rationale: The hypothesis that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy 11 (dHMN11, OMIM #620528) is driven by heterozygous loss-of-function (LoF) alleles undergoing nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)—rather than heterozygous missense or dominant-negative dimerization variants—is consistently supported by clinical genetics and molecular studies. Beijer et al. (2019) demonstrated that heterozygous nonsense mutations in SPTAN1 cause juvenile-onset dHMN, with mutant mRNA degraded by NMD leading to haploinsufficiency, whereas dominant-negative and missense mutations cluster in severe epileptic encephalopathy or spasticity phenotypes. Recent studies by De Winter et al. (2025) and Laurini et al. (2026) confirmed that heterozygous LoF alleles undergoing NMD cause a peripheral neuromuscular phenotype (with prominent distal lower limb weakness and myopathic/axonal features), confirming the molecular mechanism while refining the phenotypic spectrum.

evidence.text: Heterozygous nonsense mutations in SPTAN1 were identified in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families. Mutant mRNA containing nonsense mutations undergoes nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), resulting in reduced protein levels in patient cells, in contrast to dominant-negative mutations which cause epileptic encephalopathy phenotypes.

source.quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing... evidence.text: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 were identified in 14 families presenting with childhood-onset distal weakness and foot abnormalities. Messenger RNA and protein expression analysis confirmed nonsense-mediated decay in muscle tissue, demonstrating that LoF/NMD is the shared pathophysiologic mechanism across these distal neuromuscular presentations.

source.quote: Through international collaboration we identified 14 families with distal weakness and heterozygous SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants... Finally, we provide proof for nonsense-mediated decay in muscle tissue derived from 2 patients.

evidence.text: Heterozygous SPTAN1 nonsense and loss-of-function variants manifest with overlapping distal neuropathic and myopathic features, underscoring that loss-of-function alleles drive peripheral neuromuscular phenotypes rather than dominant-negative epileptic encephalopathy.

conflicts: Recent studies (De Winter et al. 2025, Laurini et al. 2026) report that heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 frequently show primary myopathic changes (distal myopathy with selective extensor hallucis longus and anterior compartment fatty replacement) on imaging and biopsy in addition to or instead of purely axonal motor neuronopathy, indicating that the phenotypic classification of dHMN11 vs distal myopathy represents a continuum of SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency.

new_directions.question_text: To what degree do SPTAN1 heterozygous loss-of-function alleles cause primary lower motor axonal degeneration versus primary distal skeletal muscle structural breakdown?
new_directions.rationale: Emerging findings by De Winter et al. (2025) suggest that patients previously diagnosed with dHMN11 or presenting with LoF SPTAN1 variants exhibit myopathic pathology on biopsy and specific muscle MRI patterns, suggesting haploinsufficiency may impact muscle integrity directly in addition to motor axons.
